models.title: 蛋白质分泌
models.scope: One pre-folded soluble cargo in a conventional animal-cell ER-to-Golgi-to-plasma-membrane route; cisternal maturation is a teaching model. No control branches or other roots.
checks: Inspected all zh/en stages at 0, .12, .20, .42, .67, .78, .90 and corresponding branch thresholds .34/.39/.70/.925/.963/.992; catalog cell-only registration and labels inspected. Existing screenshot at .28 inspected.
Cargo starts already folded in ER lumen. Therefore absence of an animated nascent chain/translocon is a declared upstream omission, not itself a claim that folded protein crosses the bilayer.
ER ribosomes are outside ER lumen, but the explicitly smaller subunit lies closer to membrane than the large subunit.
ER and Golgi caps are removed during transfer, yet independent mouth/neck surfaces have incompatible boundaries. Their open lumens are not connected by a single sealed surface.

During .42-.67 the tracked cargo stays on the centerline of the same moving cisterna. The cis-to-trans direction, changing cisternal identity and omitted retrograde enzyme traffic are described consistently. The moving background-cisterna reset is a schematic rather than lineage tracking.

Cargo follows a luminal carrier path and exits through the explicit plasma-membrane pore. Only one tracked cargo group persists throughout; no cargo destruction/duplication was found. The membrane itself is not persistently transferred into the surface geometry.
Coat and sorting machinery are explicitly omitted. Glycan linkage class is unspecified, so later glycan appearance cannot be treated as a confirmed N-glycosylation timing error.

sources.title: Pfeffer et al. (2015), Structure of the native Sec61 protein-conducting channel
sources.supports: Opened primary structural article. Native rough-ER ribosome-Sec61 architecture and Fig. 1/2 identify the large-subunit/translocon interface and the cytosolic orientation of the ribosome.

sources.title: The Cell — The Endoplasmic Reticulum
sources.supports: Opened chapter; conventional secretory proteins translocate into ER during synthesis and are transported onward from the luminal compartment.

sources.title: Molecular Biology of the Cell — Transport from the ER through the Golgi Apparatus
sources.supports: Opened chapter; sealed membrane-bound carriers, luminal cargo transfer, cis-to-trans traffic and cisternal maturation with retrograde enzyme recycling.

sources.title: Molecular Biology of the Cell — Molecular Mechanisms of Membrane Transport
sources.supports: Opened chapter; docking is followed by membrane fusion, preserving distinct compartments outside the specific connection.

sources.title: Molecular Biology of the Cell — Endocytosis
sources.supports: Opened chapter, endocytic-exocytic cycle section: exocytosis adds membrane to the cell surface, balancing membrane retrieval.

findings.evidence: The large ribosome mesh center is y=.89-row*.57. The explicitly named small mesh copies it then applies small.position.y-=.04. The ER lies below these meshes (first sac center y=.68; upper membrane near y=.82). Thus the small subunit is placed between the large subunit and ER, rather than offset on the cytosolic side of the large subunit. No separate Sec61 contact is modeled.
findings.whyWrong: The large subunit carries the peptide-exit tunnel and docks to the ER translocon. Inverting the two-subunit interface is a recognizable structural error even when translocation itself is omitted.
findings.fix: Orient a two-subunit ribosome with the large-subunit exit site toward the membrane and the small subunit on the cytosolic side/alongside. If adding a contact marker, attach it to the large-subunit exit site; do not expand the scene into an unrequested synthesis sequence.
findings.verification: For each ER-bound ribosome, its large-subunit exit/contact site is the membrane-facing interface and the small subunit never lies between it and the ER. Confirm in cross-section at every static ER row.

findings.location: 50-101, 174-193, 262-278, 463-503: cisterna mouth / cylindrical neck / open carrier
findings.evidence: At the ER budding mouth, the rotated cisterna opening at x=-2.03833 is an ellipse with semiaxes .08714 and .34233. erNeck is an independent open cylinder radius .15, spanning x=-2.05 to -1.79. The carrier opening has radius .20939 at x=-1.90859. No transition surface welds these incompatible loops; a back-side point such as mouth offset z=-.25 lies inside the cisterna aperture but outside the neck radius, leaving a cytosol-facing opening beyond the declared front viewing cut. Golgi mouths similarly use a flattened elliptical cisterna, .14/.19 neck and .20939 spherical carrier opening.
findings.whyWrong: Removing caps and overlapping mismatched tubes does not create one sealed lumen-to-lumen neck. These additional gaps contradict the stage promise that cargo remains in a membrane-enclosed space; they are not the named front visualization cut.
findings.fix: Construct each connected bud/fusion intermediate from a shared profile/mesh, or explicitly weld the full donor-mouth loop through a transition neck to the carrier loop. Derive all interface positions/radii from shared parameters and remove hidden internal duplicate surfaces.
findings.verification: Outside the intentionally marked viewing cut, the connected donor-neck-carrier surface has no boundary edges or uncovered aperture sectors. Cross-sectional lumen connectivity is donor-to-carrier only, never lumen-to-cytosol. Check .12-.20 and .34-.42/.67-.78, not only closed travel frames.

findings.location: 340-360, 476-485: fusion shell and plasma membrane closure
findings.evidence: At p=.90 the radius-.31 carrier and all its lipid instances are hidden; a separate radius-.4 fusion shell appears. The plasma-membrane sheets and lipid instances never change. At .992 fusion is hidden and the original closure disk reappears. Therefore none of the tracked carrier membrane elements persist in the receiving membrane, despite the final stage explicitly saying carrier membrane joins the surface.
findings.whyWrong: The cargo transfer direction is correct, but membrane incorporation is represented as object disappearance/reset. This is an important teaching ambiguity, not a demand for exact molecular-area conservation in a schematic.
findings.fix: Morph the same carrier membrane into a marked patch of the cell surface, or keep a transferred lipid patch visible after flattening. If the field of view has a lipid reservoir, make that transfer explicit; avoid replacing all membrane with the unchanged initial state.
findings.verification: Carrier-derived membrane/leaflet identity survives docking, pore opening and flattening; after cargo release there is a traceable contribution in the surface. Cargo remains a single object and the closure creates no membrane-crossing path.

limitations: Only a representative supplied image was inspected. Interface defects were derived from explicit geometric parameters, not inferred from transparency alone.
No measured rates, quantities or atomic fold claims are present. Enzyme/glycan chemistry and ER-Golgi intermediate compartments remain scoped simplifications.
No product files, tests, renderer, browser or thumbnails were changed during this Phase A audit.

models.title: 转录
models.scope: Generic eukaryotic nuclear Pol II transcription of a protein-coding gene, shared animal and plant routes; no exposed controls or organism-specific factor identities.
checks: Read catalog roots and both language versions of intro, six stages (0/.13/.27/.43/.68/.86), labels, legend and sources. All registered root contexts use the same generic nuclear mechanism.
DNA has two antiparallel backbones; local bubble tracks Pol II and reanneals behind it. Each exposed base remains on its own strand, rather than leaving an intact rung spanning the opened bubble.

RNA is one continuous backbone and nucleotide series. Before cleavage its 3′ end coincides with the active-site marker and its older 5′ end exits behind Pol II; RNA growth and template-reading directions agree with text.

Termination starts after RNA release begins; Pol II continues downstream and eventually departs while DNA recloses. Transcript release is not labeled mature mRNA; capping, splicing and polyadenylation are explicitly omitted.

At p=.86, actual instance transforms show visible main RNA and newly visible downstream remnant have coincident 3′ endpoints to 7.7e-8 scene units. Both paths use rnaPoint(distance), so their first .4 path-parameter units coincide while the full main RNA remains length 3.57. The new remnant appears before any cleavage interpolation displacement.
At p=.91 the full-length main RNA has moved away while a separate .4 remnant remains at Pol II; no existing RNA segment was removed from the released chain. At p=1 only the released chain remains.

sources.title: Barnes et al. (2015), transcribing Pol II with a complete transcription bubble, PDB 5C44
sources.supports: Opened structural record: a transcribing complex contains Pol II, template/non-template DNA and RNA; the bubble forks coordinate DNA opening/reannealing with the nascent transcript. This is conserved topology evidence, not a fitted shape for these models.

sources.title: Aibara et al. (2021), Structures of mammalian RNA polymerase II pre-initiation complexes
sources.supports: Opened article: mammalian PIC assembles on DNA; XPB translocation promotes local opening downstream of TATA. This supports the depicted order, not the invented protein folds.

sources.title: Eaton et al. (2018), Xrn2 accelerates termination by RNA polymerase II, underpinned by CPSF73 activity
sources.supports: Opened article during review (later requests intermittently blocked): CPSF73-dependent cleavage precedes degradation of polymerase-associated downstream RNA and efficient termination on most tested protein-coding genes. Cleavage partitions one existing RNA rather than copying its terminal segment.

sources.title: Larochelle et al. (2018), Common mechanism of transcription termination at coding and noncoding RNA genes in fission yeast
sources.supports: Opened full article: cleavage yields a released upstream RNA and a new uncapped downstream 5′ end. Used only for cleavage topology, not to import yeast-specific factor identities into animal/plant scenes.

findings.evidence: The main RNA is always rendered over length=.12+growth*3.45; after growth completes that is 3.57. At p>=.86 a second mesh of length .39*(1-termination)+.01 becomes visible, also starting from rnaPoint(0,...). At the .86 boundary cleavage is still zero, so this new .4 segment exactly overlays the existing RNA segment. Subsequently the complete original RNA moves away without being shortened or split at a cleavage coordinate.
findings.whyWrong: Endonucleolytic cleavage partitions one existing transcript into upstream released RNA and downstream polymerase-associated RNA, making a new downstream 5′ end. The scene instead duplicates the original near-active-site segment and then pulls the copies apart. Later downstream synthesis cannot justify the instantaneous pre-existing .4 segment at the cleavage boundary.
findings.fix: Define a cleavage coordinate on the pre-existing RNA path. Partition its backbone and nucleotides into non-overlapping upstream/downstream spans at that coordinate; preserve the downstream 3′ active-site anchor and reveal additional downstream length only as Pol II progresses. Move the released upstream product from the actual cut end.
findings.verification: Immediately before/after cleavage, each pre-existing RNA segment must belong to exactly one product, with both cut ends coincident initially. No visible RNA length/nucleotide count may jump at cleavage absent synthesis; the downstream 3′ end remains anchored while its newly created 5′ end is the cut end. Check forward and reverse seeks around .86 and .91.

limitations: No browser operated; existing p=.55 image and code-derived instanced geometry were reviewed. This is not visual acceptance of every camera angle.

Animal and plant protein-coding transcription share the coarse depicted sequence, but mammalian and yeast structural/termination evidence does not verify species-specific plant termination factors. None are named or mechanistically expanded in the model.
The review does not demand exact nucleotide counts, catalytic chemistry or omitted RNA processing; the issue is the topological duplication explicitly introduced at the cut.

models.title: 光合作用
models.scope: Legacy higher-plant chloroplast overview: light capture, thylakoid light reactions, stromal Calvin cycle and energy-carrier return. No controls.
checks: Read all 825 source lines, geometry helpers, all six stages, labels and zh/en intro/legend. Exercised stage and intermediate/end states headlessly; inspected /tmp/atlas-refinement/photosynthesis.png.

Two chloroplast envelope membranes enclose grana/thylakoids and stroma. PSII/OEC and PSI/F1 orientation were checked against the actual top-disc coordinates, rather than assuming the global y plane is the thylakoid lumen.
The plant-specific ATP synthase uses a c14 ring, unlike the new shared c10 helper. PSII dimer/OEC, PSI antenna and stromal Rubisco are distinguishable schematic assemblies.

Water/O2 is assigned to PSII light reactions; NADPH comes from the PSI side and ATP from the synthase side. Both feed stromal carbon fixation; CO2 supplies carbon, G3P is the output, and ADP/Pi/NADP+ return.

The arrows are explicitly reaction relationships rather than literal particle paths or stoichiometric counts. Cumulative stage activation does not teach a cell-wide sequential clock or a dark-only Calvin cycle.
No confirmed science defect found within this overview scope. It does not claim to resolve the detailed electron chain or proton stoichiometry.

models.title: 噬菌体侵染
models.scope: Legacy initial-entry model explicitly scoped to T4 on a Gram-negative bacterial envelope, despite being opened from the T2 structural atlas root.
checks: Read all three bilingual stages, intro, catalog summary and dependent phageDetails/microbeGeometry helpers. No condition controls or root overrides exist.
Stage 0: capsid and tail remain extracellular while fibers approach receptors. Two lipid bilayers plus peptidoglycan delimit the Gram-negative envelope.
Stage .32: sheath shortens/widens; the tail tube keeps fixed axial length and translates toward the periplasm. Cytoplasmic membrane bulges to the tip; pore seals are removed only during entry.

Stage .6/end: one contiguous arclength interval of duplex geometry passes from the capsid through the tail and channel into cytoplasm; capsid remains outside. Tail outlet/channel dimensions and alignment were traced in code.
The intro explicitly calls this T4 mechanism and excludes a precise T2 reconstruction; catalog repeats T4. Reusing a schematic T-even head silhouette does not itself assert identical T2/T4 proteins.
Read-only bundled runtime executed 0/.28/.32/.55/.6/.8/1; inspected infection.png at .55. No model/product files were written.

findings.evidence: CMG 六亚基中心位于 yz 平面半径 0.41、主椭球半径 [0.26,0.18,0.19]。helicase.position=(fork−0.04,0,0)，两条模板却按同一个对称开叉公式通过，未将前导模板送入该孔。代入 p=0.55，在 CMG 中心平面两模板径向距离约 0.391；至少一个亚基椭球归一化距离平方约 0.576<1，即 DNA 穿过蛋白体积。p=0.28 和 0.70 也出现相交。
findings.whyWrong: 画面明确标注中央通道，实际模板却穿过亚基带，且没有前导模板通过 C-tier、后随模板从叉分出的路径。错误不只是分子比例，而是马达与底物的连接拓扑。

models.title: 启动子与转录装配
models.scope: Mammalian nuclear TATA-containing protein-coding promoter; DNA and general transcription factors assemble one Pol II initiation attempt. Intact and altered-site examples are explicitly bounded, not universal mutation outcomes.

models.title: 增强子与远程调控
models.scope: Mammalian nuclear enhancer/promoter regulatory schematic on one nucleosomal fiber; coactivator-competent versus recruitment-impaired illustrative observation windows.
checks: Read both languages, all six stages (0/.17/.35/.53/.66/.8), intro, labels, legend, metadata and both coactivator settings. Same chromatin trajectory is used in both conditions.

Inspected octamer construction, duplex nucleosomal wraps, linker endpoint transforms and chromatin updates. The coarse topology is eight histones with left-handed DNA wrapping, connected by duplex linkers; enhancer and promoter are positions on the same fiber.

Activator binding is allowed in both conditions. Mediator recruitment differs; Pol II arrives in both. Competent RNA windows are [.59,.74) and [.87,.99), impaired has none. No claim that all basal transcription is zero is made.

Burst times are prescribed independently of the geometric distance. Lack of obligatory enhancer-promoter contact is not itself classified as a defect: available locus-specific live-cell evidence does not justify demanding universal instantaneous contact.

Actual RNA is single-stranded. However every linker remains paired during both bursts: chromatinGeometry.js line 175 calls dna.update(link.point), using molecularDNA default paired=()=>1. Pol II stays at a fixed offset to the promoter while RNA length increases.

Read-only world-coordinate measurement at p=.68 gives RNA 3′=(3.23734608,.26805465,-.05601349) and catalytic center=(3.26624611,.34465466,-.46656349), separation .41863358 versus catalytic radius .03465.

sources.supports: Opened structural record: eight histone subunits organize duplex DNA into a surrounding superhelix. The model reproduces that coarse topology; its individual folds and chromatin trajectory are not structure fits.

sources.supports: Opened structural record: a transcribing complex contains Pol II, template/non-template DNA and RNA; the bubble forks coordinate DNA opening/reannealing with the nascent transcript. This is conserved topology evidence, not a fitted shape for these models.

findings.kind: misleading molecular topology and missing causal engagement
findings.location: update(), lines 178-228; chromatinGeometry.js line 175; geometry.js molecularDNA default pairing at line 316
findings.evidence: The burst path is explicitly labeled nascent RNA and lengthens, but its 3′ end is .4186 units away from the displayed catalytic center. The promoter linker continues to render all base-pair bonds because no pairing/opening callback is provided. Neither template movement through Pol II nor polymerase movement along that linker accompanies the increase in RNA length.
findings.whyWrong: A literal molecular RNA elongation scene cannot show synthesis from an entirely paired, unengaged DNA duplex with its growing end outside the catalytic site. Independent burst timing is an acceptable regulatory abstraction; it does not correct the local molecular topology.
findings.fix: Either implement a local promoter transcription bubble and continuously anchored template/RNA path, with relative template/Pol II progression during a burst, or replace the literal chain with an explicitly abstract output indicator and remove the claim that this view depicts RNA molecular elongation. Preserve the two control conditions and do not invent a universal proximity trigger.
findings.verification: During each RNA growth window, assert a connected RNA 3′/catalytic anchor, exposed template in an actual local DNA bubble, and advancement relative to template bases. Outside windows, output identity/fate must be explicit. Compare both controls at identical p to retain equal chromatin geometry.

limitations: No browser operated; representative p=.55 screenshot is before RNA production, so finding comes from complete branch formulas and actual mesh sampling during a burst.

Coactivator/activator folds and whole-fiber motion are illustrative, not a fitted locus or measured stochastic process. Direct enhancer contact, every initiation factor and chromatin opening history need not all be depicted in a regulatory overview.
Released RNA is not retained between bursts. Recorded as a representation limit rather than a separate confirmed degradation claim, because output fate is not the lesson.

findings.fix: Preserve contour length while reallocating it from arms/slack into the loop, or explicitly switch this to a coarse contact-domain diagram without nucleotide-scale DNA.
findings.verification: For fixed genomic extent, total centerline contour length should be constant within chosen rendering tolerance as loop span increases; material locus order must remain fixed.

models.title: 受体介导内吞
models.scope: Mammalian LDL-receptor uptake at plasma membrane through initial acidic early-endosome sorting; no alternate controls or root contexts.
checks: Inspected every zh/en stage at 0, .14, .34, .47, .67, .8 and intermediate/end states, plus intro, labels, legend, entries and helper geometry. Existing screenshot at .26 inspected.
LDLR ectodomain/cargo face extracellular or luminal space; its short tail/adaptor face cytosol. The inward normal on detached carriers preserves this relationship.

Pit stays connected until .43; detached carrier is one bilayer. Clathrin/adaptor removal (.45-.54) precedes fusion (.67); dynamin collar lies at the bud neck. Front viewing sector is explicitly a cutaway.

Acidic early-endosome assumption is consistent with ligand release and receptor compaction; the V-ATPase head is on cytosolic side. Proton flux, ATP hydrolysis and pH are not animated, so acidification kinetics are not validated.
Fused endosome shape retains LDL in lumen and sorts receptors along a narrow membrane tubule, but three receptors collapse to identical transforms during the fusion-to-sorting interval.
No parameter-dependent controls and no non-cell roots are declared; all continuous progress branches were inspected.

sources.title: Molecular Biology of the Cell — Transport into the Cell from the Plasma Membrane: Endocytosis
sources.supports: Opened full text; LDL-receptor complexes enter coated vesicles, uncoat, release LDL in acidic early endosomes, and receptors sort into recycling tubules; V-ATPase pumps protons from cytosol to lumen.

sources.title: Molecular Biology of the Cell — Molecular Mechanisms of Membrane Transport
sources.supports: Opened full text; adaptors and clathrin act on cytosolic face, dynamin participates at neck, and coat removal follows release.

findings.evidence: When fused becomes true at p=.67, xx=1+q*1.1+sort*(1.4+i*.12). sort is zero until p=.73, so every receptor receives exactly the same xx, y=-1.25, z=-rr and rotation. Read-only sampling: receptor pair distances at .66999 were .97448/1.66217; at .67, .68, .70 and .72 both distances are 0. Cargo remains three distinct particles.
findings.whyWrong: Separate transmembrane receptors disappear into one visual object during fusion, obscuring their identity and membrane-preserving redistribution. This is a confirmed transform overlap, not evidence of actual molecular coalescence.
findings.fix: Carry each receptor from its own carrier-membrane coordinate into distinct coordinates on the fused envelope; preserve independent membrane anchors throughout acid release and tubule sorting.
findings.verification: Across .66-.96, all three receptor anchors remain on the membrane, preserve sidedness and maintain resolvable pairwise separation; no discontinuous many-to-one collapse at .67.

limitations: Only the provided .26 screenshot was inspected; other stages were evaluated by geometry/formulas and read-only Node sampling, not new browser renders.
LDLR/LDL/clathrin are declared structural schematics. Exact atomic structures, coat stoichiometry, receptor diffusion rates and proton counts are not claimed.
PMC2803231 returned an access challenge; its listed title was not treated as scientific validation. Core LDL-trafficking claims were verified through the accessible NCBI chapter.

models.title: 宏自噬
models.scope: Mammalian macroautophagy of an illustrative damaged cytosolic TPI aggregate; lysosomal cathepsin-D structural reference; no controls or alternate root contexts.
checks: Inspected all zh/en stages at 0, .16, .44, .54, .65, .79, all transitions and end state, helpers and reference-coordinate provenance. Existing screenshot at .22 inspected.

Phagophore cups connect at an open rim before .44. Outer and inner membraneSurface objects each contain two leaflet surfaces, giving the correct four-leaflet double-membrane concept; cargo is inside inner membrane on closure.

At fusion (.65), only outer autophagosomal membrane is replaced by the continuous lysosome/autophagosome envelope; inner membrane remains around cargo. Numerical profile comparison at .65-.93 found the inner sphere enclosed by the merged envelope.
Luminal glycans and cytosolic V-ATPase head have correct side assignments. Native reference identities 1HTI and 1LYA were verified on RCSB; distorted TPI aggregate is explicitly illustrative.

The degradation branch does not actually breach the inner membrane: opacity and radius change while its topology stays a sphere until it is hidden. Cargo degradation and protease access occur before removal.
No controls declared. Dynamic membrane normals and bounds were inspected as supporting geometry; userData alone was not used to infer biological correctness.

sources.title: Yim and Mizushima (2020), Lysosome biology in autophagy
sources.supports: Opened publisher full text (cookie-compatible URL). Outer membrane fusion precedes inner membrane degradation; lysosomal hydrolases gain access to autophagic cargo after the inner membrane barrier is degraded. Fig. 1 and the IAM-degradation section.

sources.title: RCSB PDB 1HTI — Human triosephosphate isomerase
sources.supports: Opened structural record; confirms the reference identity, not the illustrative damaged aggregate conformation.

sources.title: RCSB PDB 1LYA — Human cathepsin D
sources.supports: Opened structural record; confirms lysosomal protease reference identity.

findings.location: 95-111, 146-168: breakdown, inner sphere and enzyme trajectories
findings.evidence: breakdown=ease(p,.75,.96) simultaneously shrinks/fades the inner membrane, shrinks cargo and creates fragments. inner.set still uses a complete spherical profile (thetaMax=PI), and inner.mesh remains visible until p=.94. At p=.80 the inner radius is 1.2081 and opacity .8569, yet cargo degradation is .1431 and fragments are visible; every protease center remains outside (nearest 1.444). At p=.85 a cathepsin center lies 1.0627 from the autophagosome center, inside the still-closed sphere radius 1.1364 (opacity .5357). Only the permanently declared viewing cut is open.
findings.whyWrong: A transparent closed bilayer is still a barrier. The scene depicts cargo digestion before hydrolases have access, then hydrolases cross a geometrically intact inner membrane. The text instead correctly states inner-membrane degradation followed by cargo hydrolysis.
findings.fix: Give inner-membrane breakdown a real perforation/discontinuity or remove the barrier in a distinct preceding phase. Gate protease entry and cargo cleavage on accessible lumen connectivity; then degrade cargo into products while retaining the outer membrane.
findings.verification: Before inner-membrane permeability, proteases remain outside its enclosed region and cargo/fragments are unchanged. Protease paths cross only an actual breach after it exists; cargo degradation starts only after access. The visualization cut is never counted as the breach.

limitations: Native backbone identities were verified but no atom-by-atom audit of the embedded decimated coordinate arrays was attempted.
Upstream signals, membrane supply, lipid hydrolysis enzymes, metabolite export and exact mass/kinetic conservation are explicitly outside this teaching scene.
The original two PMC review links returned access challenges; a publisher-hosted authoritative review was opened and used instead.

models.title: 有丝分裂
models.scope: Mammalian somatic-cell open mitosis, starting after DNA replication; four replicated chromosomes are an explicitly declared visual subset, not a complete mammalian karyotype. Six stages; attachment control normal/unattached; no alternate root context.
checks: Read entries, both language intros/stages/legends/control labels, all update formulas, divisionShapes helper and smoke tests; inspected representative /tmp/atlas-refinement/mitosis.png. Technical smoke metadata was not accepted as biological proof.

Actual chromatid construction has four chromosome indices × two sisters = eight groups. Read-only mesh traversal across p=0,.14,.22,.28,.43,.55,.62,.70,.86,.94,1 preserves eight groups; at p=1 four single chromatids lie at each daughter side (x≈±1.94). This is the correct replicated-to-daughter chromosome accounting for the stated subset.

Normal path: nuclear-envelope breakdown precedes metaphase, sisters orient toward opposite poles, cohesion disappears as separation begins, furrow and daughter envelopes follow segregation. Division is a schematic temporal sequence, not measured kinetics.

Unattached control actually clamps effective progress to .43, shortens one capture bundle to 58%, keeps sister centres .24 apart, and prevents separation, furrowing and daughter-cell reveal even at requested p=1. Arrest is implemented in geometry, not only userData.

Checked six stage anchors and intermediate transition intervals, including nuclear-envelope crossfade, metaphase, separation and membrane completion. No replication geometry is added during mitosis; ATP chemistry is outside stated scope.

Bilingual description correctly distinguishes an unattached kinetochore from successful biorientation and discloses subset/cutaway/schematic chromatin. Actual interpolar and kinetochore geometry still have the issues below.

sources.title: Alberts et al., Molecular Biology of the Cell: Mitosis
sources.supports: Opened chapter: kinetochore capture and opposite-pole attachment; interpolar microtubules interdigitate with oppositely oriented plus ends; anaphase A/B and nuclear reassembly.

sources.title: Alberts et al., Molecular Biology of the Cell: Cytokinesis
sources.supports: Opened chapter: animal actomyosin ring, membrane ingression and completion of cytokinesis.

sources.title: Rieder et al. (1995), The checkpoint delaying anaphase in response to chromosome monoorientation is mediated by an inhibitory signal produced by unattached kinetochores
sources.supports: Opened original paper page/abstract: laser removal of the last unattached kinetochore permits anaphase in PtK1 cells, supporting the implemented arrest branch.

sources.title: Mastronarde et al. (1993), Interpolar spindle microtubules in PTK cells; DOI 10.1083/jcb.123.6.1475
sources.supports: Retrieved and read primary article XML/abstract: electron-microscopy reconstructions identify interdigitating interpolar arrays and antiparallel nearest neighbours. The old scanned article XML exposes abstract text, not a complete machine-readable results section.

findings.evidence: Each of eight overlap bundles is built from three continuous strands spanning -0.94*poleX to +0.94*poleX. setBundle constructs 12 consecutive cylinders per strand across the whole interval; it creates neither two half-spindle populations nor plus ends terminating within an overlap region. These strands remain continuous during pole separation.
findings.whyWrong: The lesson depicts interpolar microtubules as individual pole-to-pole cables. Mammalian interpolar arrays contain interdigitating antiparallel microtubules; their overlap and relative sliding are central to the claimed spindle architecture. A continuous strand is not the topology of the two overlapping populations.
findings.fix: Construct two opposed sets with separate plus-end terminations in a shared midzone; connect/crosslink the overlapping portions schematically and animate their relative movement during spindle elongation. Do not require every minus end to be located exactly at the centrosome.
findings.verification: Inspect actual strand endpoints at metaphase and anaphase: no individual interpolar strand spans both poles, opposing populations overlap in the midzone, and overlap/sliding changes coherently with pole distance.

findings.evidence: Attached bundle endpoints use world offsets x=chromatid.x+side*.19,z=chromatid.z+.06 rather than the transformed layered kinetochore surface. A read-only nearest-triangle probe of the first fully captured strand at p=.43 and .55 gives endpoint-to-kinetochore distance≈.03158 with fibre radius .009, leaving approximately .0226 clear space. Probe includes outer/inner plates and interface rods, not userData.
findings.whyWrong: The normal branch is labelled attached and checkpoint satisfied but an explicitly drawn fibre ends visibly short of the explicitly drawn attachment interface. This is an attachment ambiguity rather than evidence that the biological checkpoint logic is wrong.
findings.fix: Expose a local outer-kinetochore attachment anchor and transform it through the chromatid world matrix for the bundle target; ensure the radius contacts the interface. Keep the unattached condition distinctly short.
findings.verification: At fully captured metaphase and separated states, test bundle end surfaces intersect the intended transformed kinetochore interface within rendering tolerance; the blocked fibre must remain separated.

limitations: No browser operation or complete multi-angle visual acceptance was performed; the local screenshot is one representative frame. Mesh/formula checks cover all declared stages and the only control.

The chromosome/fibre models are coarse teaching meshes, not atomistic structures. This audit does not reject disclosed spatial-scale compression, reduced chromosome count, open-front cutaways or omitted biochemical detail.

models.title: 减数分裂
models.scope: Mouse primary spermatocyte with two depicted autosomal homolog pairs, starting after S phase and ending as four connected haploid spermatids, not mature sperm. Seven stages; no user control or alternate root context is declared.
checks: Read entries, both language intros/stages/legends, all update formulas and helper geometry; inspected representative /tmp/atlas-refinement/meiosis.png. Scope disclosure correctly says two pairs are a subset and that mature sperm are not produced by this scene.

Actual construction is two homolog pairs × two homologs × two sisters = eight chromatids. Read-only traversal across p=0,.14,.22,.28,.43,.55,.62,.70,.86,.94,1 preserves all eight. After I each side contains two dyads/four chromatids; at final x≈±2.05,y≈±1.25 each of four products contains two single chromosomes, one of each depicted pair.

Homologs separate in I while sisters retain paired geometry and the centromeric-cohesion marker; sister kinetochores orient to the same pole in I and opposite poles in II. No chromosome duplication or second DNA replication occurs between divisions.

Reciprocal distal recolouring affects one nonsister chromatid from each homolog within each pair. Two recombinants per pair and two unchanged sisters are retained in the correct final products. The chromosome-arm geometry at the exchange site is nevertheless misleading, as documented below.
The choice to orient both parental-colour homologs to the same side in I is one possible assortment, not a count error; text does not claim to enumerate all assortment outcomes.

Read every stage anchor and transition: synapsis/crossing-over, I spindle, I segregation/furrow, II spindle without replication, II segregation/furrow and final nuclei. No checkpoint intervention control is declared, so this depicts an unperturbed route rather than a test of arrest.

Three retained bridge objects yield a connected four-cell lineage graph at the end, consistent with male germ-cell incomplete cytokinesis in principle. Their actual membrane/channel topology is not correctly built.

Chinese and English agree about mouse scope, homolog-vs-sister separation, lack of intervening replication, retained bridges and spermatid endpoints. The stated mouse scope conflicts with the shared chromosome shape.

sources.title: Cooper, The Cell: Meiosis and Fertilization
sources.supports: Opened chapter: synapsis aligns homologous chromosomes; chiasmata mark sites of crossing over; homologs segregate in I, sisters in II without another replication round.

sources.title: Kim et al. (2015), Meikin is a conserved regulator of meiosis-I-specific kinetochore function
sources.supports: Opened original Nature article abstract: mouse MEIKIN promotes sister-kinetochore mono-orientation and centromeric cohesion protection in meiosis I.

sources.title: Mouse Genetics, Jackson Laboratory: The mouse karyotype
sources.supports: Opened authoritative chapter: standard mouse autosomes and X are telocentric; Robertsonian chromosome races are a specifically described exception, not the unstated default.

sources.title: Kalitsis et al. (2006), Mouse telocentric sequences reveal a high rate of homogenization and possible role in Robertsonian translocation
sources.supports: Retrieved and read original-paper abstract via Europe PMC: sequencing of mouse telocentric ends places telomere and centromere sequences only 1.8–11 kb apart, supporting a terminal centromere rather than two comparable arms.

sources.title: Greenbaum et al. (2006), TEX14 is essential for intercellular bridges and fertility in male mice
sources.supports: Retrieved and read original-paper abstract via Europe PMC: incomplete male germ-cell cytokinesis leaves a large cytoplasmic channel. Supports persistent communication, not a solid tether between sealed cells.

findings.evidence: Both mouse autosomal pairs use the shared chromatid helper: one arm extends from -.76L to the centromere at 0, the other from 0 to +L. Thus the depicted short arm occupies about 43% of chromosome length, with a conspicuously internal centromere on every chromosome.
findings.whyWrong: The standard mouse autosomal complement is telocentric. Two nearly comparable arms falsely depict the explicitly selected mouse specimen. Robertsonian mouse races can have fused metacentric chromosomes, but no such strain or fusion scope is declared; the reduced-count disclaimer does not resolve morphology.
findings.fix: Use a meiosis-specific telocentric chromosome parameter/shape placing the centromere close to one end, retaining matched homolog lengths, sister cohesion and the existing count. Alternatively, only if intentionally changing the specimen, explicitly document a scientifically supported Robertsonian karyotype and adapt homolog pairing accordingly.
findings.verification: Measure rendered arm lengths relative to the centromere for both homolog pairs; verify a terminal/near-terminal centromere for the declared standard mouse scope while keeping eight chromatids and correct I/II allocation.

findings.evidence: The exchanged distal mesh begins at local y=.69L. The two gold chiasma cylinders form an X at y=.84L, with ends at .69L and .99L on opposite homolog sides. Chromosome arm meshes remain intact and simply swap distal materials. The fixed synapsis rungs at x=±.32 likewise do not derive endpoints from the homolog axes.
findings.whyWrong: The supposed exchange junction and the ancestry boundary are at different loci, and the connecting X joins unequal longitudinal positions on opposite homologs. This shows an arbitrary bridge plus recolouring instead of a crossover between aligned homologous loci of two nonsister chromatids.
findings.fix: Create a shared exchange coordinate on both aligned homolog axes; use it for the material breakpoint and connected/deformed nonsister chromatid paths. Anchor synapsis rungs to their actual paired axes. Retain reciprocal exchange without creating or deleting chromatid material.
findings.verification: At crossover, extract world-space exchange endpoints and ancestry boundaries: they must meet at matched homologous coordinates within tolerance, affect exactly two nonsister chromatids in the same pair, and remain continuous into the final reciprocal products.

findings.evidence: Retained bridges are k.line objects using closed CylinderGeometry, drawn between separately crossfaded daughter-cell ellipsoids. Cell membrane triangles are cut away only by front/back z, with no bridge-mouth apertures. The final connector is a capped solid cylinder and the daughter membranes have no channel openings at its endpoints.
findings.whyWrong: A male germ-cell intercellular bridge is a patent cytoplasmic channel bounded by membrane, allowing continuity between cells. A solid tether between otherwise sealed membranes conveys the wrong topology even though the text correctly says incomplete cytokinesis.
findings.fix: Model membrane necks with open lumens and matching apertures in the daughter surfaces, retaining the existing lineage connections. The open-front cutaway can expose the shared cytoplasmic channel without needing molecular TEX14 detail.
findings.verification: Cross-section each bridge and verify a continuous path between adjacent cell interiors with no membrane cap across the lumen; verify four final cells remain connected by the three retained channels.

findings.evidence: The I and II bundle targets are hardcoded offsets (x+homolog*.19,y,.3) and (x,y+sister*.19,.3). A read-only nearest-triangle probe finds≈.03158 from the first nominally attached strand endpoint to the kinetochore surfaces at p=.32 (I) and p=.68 (II), while the fibre radius is .009. The II target is not derived from the rotated chromatid matrix.
findings.whyWrong: Both meiotic stages claim attachment yet the drawn fibre terminates short of the layered kinetochore. Sister-pole orientation logic is correct, but the geometry weakens that explanation and is fragile under rotation/scale changes.
findings.fix: Use the transformed local kinetochore attachment anchor for each sister in I and II, accounting for chromatid rotation and scale, while retaining co-orientation in I and biorientation in II.
findings.verification: Assert surface contact for attached fibres in both divisions and through rotation; separately assert same-pole sister connections in I and opposite-pole sister connections in II using actual bundle endpoints.

limitations: No browser operation or complete multi-angle visual acceptance was performed; screenshot evidence is limited to one representative frame. Formula and mesh checks span all seven stages and the absence of controls/context variants was verified.

Primary mouse morphology and bridge papers were read through their original-paper abstracts returned by Europe PMC; direct PMC page access challenged the client. No unseen results or figures are claimed as reviewed.
This review does not require a full 20-pair mouse karyotype, exhaustive independent-assortment outcomes, mature sperm differentiation, atomic cohesin architecture or an unrequested arrest control.

models.title: 谷氨酸突触传递
models.scope: Mammalian central glutamatergic synapse: presynaptic terminal, extracellular cleft, postsynaptic dendrite and astrocyte. Available/blocked presynaptic calcium; no other contexts.
checks: Reviewed all six bilingual stages, labels, geometry including omega fusion shell, bilayer plugs, pore helper, every trajectory and both calcium conditions. Sampled 26 boundary/midpoint/end states; inspected provided p=.55 screenshot.

Correct global order: terminal signal then Ca influx then fusion. Blocking calcium preserves the arrival signal but prevents fusion, release and postsynaptic current. ATP/底物化学步骤、跨膜转运细节和真实速率不在该介观模型中；现有来源仅支持所检查方向和调控区别。
本结论不表示所有植物组织都适用相同壁排列。

models.title: 被子植物双受精
models.scope: 拟南芥多细胞胚珠，母方两个极核已融合为 2n 中央核；不是通用单细胞植物模型。
checks: 已检查 entries.js 中中英 intro、六个 stages、labels/legend、controls、root 声明，以及对应 Process.js / structuralDetail.js 的实际几何和 update。检查阶段边界、边界前帧、0/1 和关键过渡帧；查看已有 /tmp/atlas-refinement/<id>.png，未启动浏览器。
六阶段 p=0/.17/.33/.5/.73/.88；assignment=frontEgg/frontCentral 均检查，共 30 个采样，另重点检查 .725/.89/.91；唯一 root=plant。
珠被缺口在珠孔侧，花粉管从该缺口抵达接受助细胞；营养核领先，两个精细胞由管运送而非自行游动。释放至卵与中央细胞边界，随后短暂停留再融合。
两个控制仅交换精细胞落点，未宣称前后精细胞有固定命运；n+n→2n 合子、母方 2n+n→3n 胚乳的文字和目标分配正确。
反足细胞已退化的省略在特定物种/时间背景中说明，未把省略认定为必需补齐的缺陷；末段早期胚形态与过渡核数存在以下问题。

sources.title: Hamamura et al. (2011), Live-cell imaging reveals the dynamics of two sperm cells during double fertilization in Arabidopsis thaliana
sources.supports: 已打开 PubMed 原始活细胞成像摘要。花粉管运送两个不自行游动的精细胞，营养核领先；释放后停留于配子边界；无固定受精先后与精细胞命运偏好。

sources.title: Kimata et al. (2016), Cytoskeleton dynamics control the first asymmetric cell division in Arabidopsis zygote
sources.supports: 已打开 PMC 原始研究全文及图 1。拟南芥合子首次不对称分裂形成较小顶端细胞和较大基部细胞，分别进入胚体与胚柄相关谱系。

findings.evidence: 末段 p≥.9 显示两个尺度完全相同 [.26,.22,.18] 的细胞，中心 y=−1.1/−.74，胞体还有 0.08 的 y 重叠。intro 指定拟南芥；该组对象作为两细胞早期胚输出。
findings.whyWrong: 拟南芥正常第一次合子分裂明显不对称，形成小的顶端细胞和大的基部细胞。等大的两细胞形象会把具体物种的重要早期极性画错；简化声明不足以改变这点。
findings.fix: 画出具有独立边界的小顶端/大基部两细胞胚，基部朝珠孔、顶端朝胚囊内部；若不展示该后续过程，可将终点收敛到单个 2n 合子。
findings.verification: 若保留分裂终点，基部细胞体积大于顶端，边界不重叠且各一核 2n，方向与珠孔一致；不要改动已正确的双受精倍性。

findings.evidence: 传入精细胞自带父方核 glyph，p<.73 仍显示；独立产物父方核 spermMarkers 从 p≥.72 开始显示。p=.725 两套同时可见，合计四个父方核图形，没有标明是同一核的转移残影。
findings.whyWrong: 真实过程只有两个精细胞提供父方核。虽然后续 2n/3n 标签正确，过渡帧的重复身份仍可能被理解为额外父方核；此项是表达歧义，不是倍性计算错误。
findings.fix: 复用同两个父方核对象，或将进入态与产物态可见区间做互斥交接；核融合过渡需保持身份连续。
findings.verification: .70–.75 密集采样：在核复制前最多两个可识别父方核贡献，两个 assignment 选项结果相同；避免用只查最终 userData 的测试。

limitations: 双受精路线和倍性通过不等于后续胚发育几何通过。
配子及核采用剖面/半透明轮廓，未声称膜融合蛋白构象或核膜融合的精细分子模拟。
只检查拟南芥已融合极核场景，不能泛化为所有被子植物中央细胞初始核态。

models.title: 丝状真菌的菌丝顶端生长
models.scope: Neurospora crassa 有隔菌丝顶端生长，挂在 yeast 图谱入口；intro 明确不是出芽酵母。
checks: 已检查 entries.js 中中英 intro、六个 stages、labels/legend、controls、root 声明，以及对应 Process.js / structuralDetail.js 的实际几何和 update。检查阶段边界、边界前帧、0/1 和关键过渡帧；查看已有 /tmp/atlas-refinement/<id>.png，未启动浏览器。
六阶段 p=0/.16/.32/.49/.67/.87；delivery=normal/reduced 全覆盖，共 30 个采样；唯一 root=yeast，其物种特化说明在中英文均存在，未误判入口名称为物种宣称。
Spitzenkörper 是分层小/大囊泡群，无虚构包围膜；运输总体朝尖端，膜合酶在尖端附近、产物在胞外，隔膜孔与多核背景符合示意范围。
reduced 将递送数量/速度和延伸量降到示意比例 .24；未宣称为实测抑制剂效应或数值定律。
囊泡 update 在隔膜附近将 y/z 收拢至孔中心，但该处理不作用于实际运输轨道；已沉积聚合物也没有留在后方，详见下列条目。

sources.title: Riquelme et al. (2014), The Neurospora crassa exocyst complex tethers Spitzenkörper vesicles to the apical plasma membrane during polarized growth
sources.supports: 已打开 PubMed 原始研究摘要。分层 Spitzenkörper 囊泡群与顶端质膜的定向分泌，exocyst 参与系留。

sources.title: Delgado-Álvarez et al. (2014), Septum Development in Neurospora crassa: The Septal Actomyosin Tangle
sources.supports: 已打开 PLOS 原始研究全文。引言与成像图指出隔膜具有中心孔供胞质/细胞器联系，隔膜形成涉及质膜内陷及壁构建；实体壁不能作为胞质运输通道。

sources.title: Hunsley and Kay (1976), Wall Structure of the Neurospora Hyphal Apex
sources.supports: 已打开期刊原始研究摘要。顶端与成熟侧壁结构/厚度不同，支持顶端新生壁向侧壁成熟的区分；本论文摘要不直接给出单根聚合物运动轨迹。

findings.evidence: 隔膜位于 x=−2.8/−1.4，RingGeometry 内径参数为半径 .18（两侧面 .19）。两条运输轨道恒位于 y=±.42,z=−.13 并横贯 x=−1.4；其径向距离 sqrt(.42²+.13²)=.43966，穿过实体隔膜，远在中心孔之外。囊泡收拢算法没有改变轨道。
findings.whyWrong: 隔膜中心孔是胞质连续/交换通道，实体壁并非运输通道。画出穿壁的细胞骨架路径使区室联系与墙体屏障相互矛盾。
findings.fix: 将轨道限制在单一胞质区室，或用连续曲线穿过真实中心孔并计入轨道半径；允许用不同区室的独立轨道接续囊泡运输。
findings.verification: 所有轨道/囊泡与隔膜 slab 相交的采样点，其径向位置加自身半径应落在实际孔净半径内；实体隔膜不被胞质轨道贯穿。

findings.evidence: 同一批 15 个 deposits 每帧以 tip+.775·cosθ 定位，没有出生/固定的壁坐标。θ=0 的同一束从 p=.4 的 x≈2.0472 移到 p=.8 的 x≈3.2638，始终随顶端前进；末阶段却解释新生壁成为侧壁。
findings.whyWrong: 若这些具名对象表示已经沉积的壁聚合物，动画将其误示为与尖端一起运输的活动货物；如果只是当前合成位点，身份和壁成熟过程未说明。因此按 P2 表达歧义记录，不将省略分子级壁力学夸大成 P1。
findings.fix: 新增少量预分配出生批次，沉积后保持壁材料坐标并留在尖端后方；或明确区分移动的合成位点提示和留存的壁材料，保留可追踪的新壁→侧壁关系。
findings.verification: 选定已沉积材料标记，尖端继续前进时它留在后方/合理壁材料坐标，而非每帧强制跟尖端平移；normal/reduced 两模式均验证。

limitations: 真菌特化物种已说明；不据此声称 Saccharomyces cerevisiae 有同样的有隔菌丝结构。
不显示新隔膜生成、分支或核分裂；这些是明确范围省略，不要求增加新过程。
顶端聚合物修法需保持示意尺度，不把固定绝对坐标当作真实壁永不变形的物理定律。

models.title: 生长素：解除转录抑制
models.scope: Arabidopsis thaliana shoot-cell nuclear TIR1/AFB–SCF–Aux/IAA–activating-ARF response; separate later differential-elongation inset.
checks: Read both languages for intro, all six stages, single auxin present/low control, all labels, entries and metadata; no extra root contexts exist.
Traced SCF receptor/ASK1/cullin/RBX/E2 geometry, repressor/PB1/degron path, ARF retention, proteasome 4x7 core and 6-fold ATPase cap, ubiquitin objects, dynamic DNA/RNA, and tissue inset.
Evaluated p=0,.16,.30,.34,.45,.52,.55,.61,.65,.68,.71,.75,.88,1 for both control values; inspected /tmp/atlas-refinement/auxin.png at representative p=.55.

Low auxin correctly keeps repressor and suppresses modeled induced RNA/growth; auxin has recognition→tagging→proteasome→transcription→later growth order. ARF remains DNA-associated; degradation does not target ARF.

DNA is a two-backbone helix with a local opening; nascent RNA is a single chain originating near the polymerase. No translation occurs in the nuclear view. The explicit strand polarities are metadata/text rather than atom-level chemistry.
ATP-dependent ubiquitin activation and proteasome mechanics are not quantitatively modeled; four drawn ubiquitins are explicitly schematic, not a fixed biological chain-length claim.

sources.title: Tan et al. (2007), TIR1–ASK1–auxin–Aux/IAA structural dataset and primary-paper abstract
sources.supports: Opened the structure page and its primary-paper abstract. Auxin is anchored at the bottom of one TIR1 surface pocket; the Aux/IAA degron docks above it and closes the hormone-binding site. Arabidopsis TIR1, ASK1 and an IAA7 peptide are identified in the structure.

sources.title: Yao and Cohen (2002), A cryptic protease couples deubiquitination and degradation by the proteasome
sources.supports: Opened and read abstract: 19S recognizes ubiquitin chains, substrate unfolds for axial translocation, and POH1/Rpn11 removes substrate-attached ubiquitin during degradation. This supports conserved proteasomal chemistry, not an Arabidopsis-specific kinetic claim.

sources.title: Spartz et al. (2014), SAUR inhibition of PP2C-D phosphatases activates plasma membrane H+-ATPases
sources.supports: Opened the full primary paper. SAUR action links PP2C-D inhibition with H+-ATPase activation and cell expansion in Arabidopsis, supporting the later shoot-growth inset as a qualified downstream summary.

findings.evidence: TIR1 is an open annular LRR extrusion centered at (-2.3,1.25,0), inner radii .48/.59, with no pocket floor. Bound auxin is centered at (-2.31,1.25,.35), radius .105, inside the through-hole. At p=.40 a read-only traversal evaluated THREE.Triangle.closestPointToPoint against every transformed triangle in the entire receptor subtree, including LRR and F-box detail: minimum center-to-triangle distance .4648539527, so the radius-adjusted receptor–ligand surface gap is .3598539527. Thus the ligand is genuinely suspended away from every modeled receptor surface; this is not a nearest-vertex approximation. The same open-ring topology is visible in the supplied screenshot.
findings.whyWrong: The central teaching claim is molecular glue within a shared receptor/substrate surface pocket. A through-hole with a floating ligand fails to show receptor–auxin contact and falsely presents the recognition topology; the correct text does not repair that geometry.
findings.fix: Replace the open central aperture with a bounded concave TIR1 binding surface/pocket floor. Place auxin against that surface and bring the Aux/IAA degron over the same ligand. Keep other LRR features schematic, and preserve the later release toward the proteasome.
findings.verification: At the fully bound stage, inspect receptor pocket, auxin and degron together from two angles; the ligand must contact the depicted pocket and be capped by the degron without a clear through-hole below it. In the low-auxin condition neither ternary contact nor ubiquitin tagging should be shown.

findings.evidence: The four original ubiquitin beads remain children of the shrinking repressor. tags.visible is determined solely by tag>.05 and never detached during degradation. At p=.65 the tagged repressor remains visible at scale .5 while all four separately allocated recycledUbiquitin beads are also visible. The original chain shrinks with the substrate until the repressor disappears.
findings.whyWrong: The animation represents the same illustrated ubiquitin pool twice and lets the attached copy be consumed with Aux/IAA. Deubiquitination/recycling is explicitly taught in stage 4, so this is not just an omitted pathway: the visible transition conflicts with that claim.
findings.fix: Transfer the existing chain/beads from substrate to the proteasome-associated recycling path, or make mutually exclusive linked states for each illustrated ubiquitin. Remove its substrate attachment before its recycled representation appears; keep ubiquitin scale independent of substrate unfolding/degradation.
findings.verification: Across dense p=.60–.70 samples each of the four illustrated ubiquitins must have exactly one visible state (attached or recycled), with no disappearing attached duplicate; only the Aux/IAA substrate becomes unfolded peptide/fragments.

limitations: Source nature05731 was blocked by Nature authentication; the opened primary structural deposition provides the Tan paper abstract and composition. The Winkler article full-text endpoint failed; it was not treated as independently opened verification.
The proteasome deubiquitination source is a conserved eukaryotic mechanism study rather than plant-specific dynamics. No fixed rates or stoichiometric expression output are inferred.
The existing p=.55 image is a representative frame only. All stages were traced and evaluated in Node, but no new browser view was generated.
models.reviewer: p_operons (independent module author; Phase A read-only product audit)

models.title: 植物防御：识别 flg22
models.scope: Arabidopsis plasma-membrane FLS2–BAK1–BIK1–RBOHD branch of pattern-triggered immunity; external flg22; cytosolic kinase/electron donor; apoplastic ROS output.
checks: Read both languages for all six stages, flg22/absent control, intro, labels, source metadata and plant-only entry; no alternate root contexts exist.
Traced paired lipid heads at y=+/-.24 and tails toward midplane; FLS2/BAK1 ectodomains are at y>0 and kinase domains at y<0. flg22 never crosses the bilayer.

RBOHD has six membrane helices with alternating loops, two heme discs, cytosolic FAD/NADPH domains and N-terminal EF-hand cartoons. BIK1 remains cytosolic; electron motion is cytosol-to-apoplast and the ROS particles originate above the membrane.

Evaluated the same stage boundaries and intermediate progress values as auxin for both ligand options, plus p=.40,.41,.45,.48,.49,.60,.68 contact/motion checks. Inspected /tmp/atlas-refinement/plantDefense.png at p=.55.

No-ligand condition suppresses recruitment, phosphomarks and modeled ROS; the text correctly limits this to induced output rather than claiming zero basal activity. Calcium and parallel pathways are expressly omitted, with BIK1 not described as the sole ROS input.

flg22 is drawn with 12 coarse peptide markers rather than an atom/residue count; neither text nor metadata claims these are 12 residues. The primary source correctly defines flg22 as 22 residues. ATP/NADPH stoichiometry and O2 consumption are not counted; the diagram is not a chemical mass-balance simulation.

sources.title: Sun et al. (2013), Structural basis for flg22-induced activation of the Arabidopsis FLS2–BAK1 immune complex
sources.supports: Opened and read abstract. flg22 binds the inner FLS2 LRR surface; BAK1 contacts FLS2 and the C-terminal part of receptor-bound flg22. Complex formation supports reciprocal receptor activation.

sources.title: FLS2–BAK1–flg22 ectodomain crystal structure
sources.supports: Opened deposited primary structural dataset. The peptide is a 22-residue chain and forms a heteromeric ectodomain recognition complex. This dataset does not establish intracellular kinase coordinates.

sources.title: Li et al. (2014), FLS2-associated BIK1 directly phosphorylates RbohD
sources.supports: Opened and read abstract. Receptor-complex BIK1 directly phosphorylates RbohD at specific sites, in a calcium-independent phosphorylation mechanism, enhancing ROS output; additional calcium signaling is also present.

sources.title: Wong et al. (2007), Regulation of rice NADPH oxidase by Rac binding to its N-terminal extension
sources.supports: Opened paper record and figure captions. Plant Rboh architecture includes a cytoplasmic N-terminal EF-hand region, six transmembrane domains, and FAD/NADPH-binding regions. Used only for conserved family architecture, not to substitute rice Rac regulation for the Arabidopsis BIK1 branch.

findings.evidence: BAK1 recruitment moves only the rigid whole receptor to x=-3.3, while FLS2 remains at x=-2. Their intracellular kinase domains never move into a common interface, yet receptor phosphomarks appear once join>.65. At p=.49, closest sampled kinase vertices remain ~.674 scene units apart; FLS2 upper-domain x bounds are -2.385 to -1.7433 and BAK1 upper-domain bounds -3.59 to -3.0506. BIK1 at (-1.35,-1.25,.22) is already marked phosphorylated before its later RBOHD-directed movement, without a receptor-contact transition.
findings.whyWrong: The extracellular complex supports a physical kinase activation relay, not phosphorylation across empty cytoplasm. The current animation declares receptor/BIK1 activation while the intracellular interaction needed to convey it is geometrically absent. Ectodomain-only structural evidence must not be used as proof of the hard-coded kinase arrangement.
findings.fix: Introduce flexible juxtamembrane connections and move/rotate the kinase lobes into a readable transient contact configuration after ectodomain recruitment; stage BIK1 docking/phosphorylation at that complex before its release toward RBOHD. Alternatively show an explicitly separated intracellular interaction inset with actual contact, rather than distant phosphomarks.
findings.verification: For every induced frame where a new phosphomark appears, its donor and substrate must have a depicted contact/interface or an explicit correctly connected interaction inset. No phosphomark should appear before that contact, and the no-ligand control must remain unactivated. Validate ectodomain contact and correct membrane sides independently.

findings.evidence: Lipid exclusions are fixed at both BAK1 start (x≈0) and final (x≈-3.3) sites. During recruitment z=sin(join*pi)*.72; at p=.41 the BAK1 transmembrane helix center is z=.72, beyond the displayed lipid-row centers (maximum .54, heads reach about .61). Both unused holes remain open while the receptor takes this detour.
findings.whyWrong: This is a finite-patch rendering inconsistency rather than evidence that the biological receptor leaves the cellular membrane. Nevertheless, the visible bilayer ceases to support the moving transmembrane protein, and unexplained empty holes make the teaching view ambiguous about receptor lateral recruitment and membrane continuity.
findings.fix: Keep the receptor inside an adequately sized depicted bilayer and animate its local lipid exclusion, or choose a shorter membrane-contained path. Remove unused start/end gaps when unoccupied.
findings.verification: At dense recruitment samples, the transmembrane span must stay in the displayed membrane patch, its ectodomain remain apoplastic, and all unoccupied excluded slots be filled. Confirm no pre-cut empty pore remains in either control.

limitations: Intracellular FLS2/BAK1/BIK1 contacts are inferred from interaction/activation biology; the 4MN8 structure resolves ectodomains, not a fitted kinase arrangement. The finding does not prescribe atomically exact distances.
RBOHD six-helix/fold topology is a schematic. Rice Rboh evidence was used only for family-level architecture; Arabidopsis BIK1 causality is supported by the opened Li study.

The Kadota PubMed endpoint returned no readable content; it was not counted as independently verified primary evidence. Oxygen substrate, proton balance, ROS interconversion and other immune branches remain acknowledged teaching abstractions.
Existing screenshot is a single time point; code/runtime coverage includes all controls and stages, with no browser mutation.

models.title: 质子梯度驱动蔗糖摄取
models.scope: Arabidopsis leaf-vein companion-cell plasma membrane; ATP-driven outward H+ pumping followed by inward H+/sucrose symport.
checks: Read all six bilingual stages, intro, labels, energy control, entry metadata, anatomy.js protein/helix helpers and every update formula. No alternative root context is declared.
Direction is correct: protons move y=-1.45 to +1.2 at the pump; sucrose/proton move from positive to negative y at SUC2. ATP domains are cytosolic. SUC2 has no ATP hydrolysis event.
Both available and depleted conditions were evaluated at every stage boundary and final state. Initially unenergized depleted control prevents net uptake; ligand approach alone remains possible.
The p=0.55 local screenshot agrees with code: one ADP/Pi depiction, nine outward protons, cylindrical helices with same-side top connectors.

sources.title: Pedersen et al. 2007, Crystal structure of the plasma membrane proton pump
sources.supports: Opened primary-paper PDF: ten transmembrane helices and three cytoplasmic N/P/A domains; connected polypeptide topology; ATP-coupled H+ export. The primary paper reports one proton per ATP.

sources.title: Bavnhøj et al. 2023, Structure and sucrose binding mechanism of the plant SUC1 sucrose transporter
sources.supports: Opened publisher full text, especially Fig. 1e and Results: twelve helices in two six-helix domains connected by a cytoplasmic linker, proton-dependent uptake and alternating access. This is SUC-family structural support, not an experimentally resolved SUC2 model.

findings.location: create: pump connectors lines 83-93; SUC2 connectors lines 158-176
findings.evidence: Every connector joins the positive-y end of one TM helix to the positive-y end of the next. SUC2 creates all five links per six-helix bundle at y=0.57..0.65; pump likewise uses y=0.55..0.65. Internal helix tops therefore receive two neighboring links while lower ends dangle. This is visibly rendered at all progress values, not just metadata.
findings.whyWrong: A single transmembrane polypeptide must traverse the membrane and connect successive ends according to its topology. The rendered top-end necklace gives a branched/incorrect backbone, not merely a stylized fold. Both cited structures provide experimentally supported membrane topology.
findings.fix: Rebuild loop attachments from a verified topology map, including cytoplasmic domain/linker insertions. Alternatively omit unsupported interhelix connectors and explicitly keep only a helix-domain schematic.
findings.verification: For any connectors presented as one peptide backbone, the connectivity graph must have two terminal ends and no branch degree above two; successive TM helix endpoints and intervening loops must match the verified topology and membrane side.

findings.evidence: Nine individual H+ spheres all cross the pump from cytosol to apoplast. There is one ATP glyph with three phosphate spheres, and only phosphate[2] detaches once. The same complete clip therefore visually couples a single ATP hydrolysis to nine H+ exports.
findings.whyWrong: The isolated PM H+-ATPase pump cycle is conventionally one H+ per ATP. The numerical molecular glyphs invite an incorrect 9:1 reading even though the intended scene compresses multiple cycles. Shape/time simplification does not explain this multiplicity.
findings.fix: Animate matching ATP cycles for the exported protons, or track one ATP and one translocated H+ while representing the background gradient as a clearly distinct continuous field/pool.
findings.verification: Tracked hydrolyzed ATP and tracked exported H+ should have a 1:1 cycle correspondence, or background concentration symbols must be explicitly non-stoichiometric and not all pass through one tracked hydrolysis event.

limitations: No atomistic fit is claimed. The source structure is SUC1 whereas the transport process is SUC2; use family-level topology only.
Sucrose is represented as a generic two-ring glyph, with stereochemistry omitted; no atom-resolved validation was performed.
Only the existing representative screenshot was inspected; no browser operation.

models.title: 胞间连丝的选择性通行
models.scope: One enlarged plasmodesma between Arabidopsis root cells, with a compressed ER desmotubule and a callose-regulated cytoplasmic sleeve.
checks: Read all six zh/en stages, intro, labels, open/callose controls and all geometry/update code including dynamic leaflet/ring/instance updates.

Outer sleeve radius is 0.84 and restricted neck radius 0.49; small solute centers at radial distance about 0.57 and sphere radius 0.095 fit the open sleeve and remain outside the appressed ER. Late restricted molecules stop on the donor side.
Compressed ER connects to cortical ER branches on both sides. Transport follows the sleeve, not the ER lumen, and never requires crossing the continuous PM.
At p=1 the open condition delivers four tracked small solutes; callose condition delivers the earlier solute and blocks the later three. The bulky untargeted probe remains excluded in both.

models.title: 草履虫接合与核更新
models.scope: P. caudatum conjugation through postzygotic nuclear differentiation; subsequent two vegetative fissions omitted.
checks: Read all seven bilingual stages, intro, labels, root entry and sources; no controls or root overrides.

findings.evidence: incoming is a world-origin duplex with upper centerline y=2.45, but update sets incoming.scale.y=entry.
